newsitem.title: USA: Madonna's early songs released for first time.
newsitem.headline: Madonna's early songs released for first time.

text.p: Madonna has topped the pop music charts for over a decade by carefully crafting her image, but a newly released recording called "Pre-Madonna" gives fans rare insight into the Material Girl's early days.
The CD, which recently went on sale, features seven never-before heard Madonna songs, including the four that helped her secure a recording contract.

The record was the brainchild of co-songwriter and producer Stephen Bray, who recorded the songs with Madonna from 1980 to 1981 in New York and is credited with helping her create her distinctive sound.
Madonna's spokewoman declined to comment on the CD, which was released by the mail-order label "1-800-HARMONY" and which is also available in some stores.
The project started out as a simple archiving project when Bray realised he should transfer the deteriorating magnetic tape recordings to a newer digital format.

"I realised that if I'm doing all this work ... maybe other people will like this too," Bray said in an interview. "It was very nostalgic and enjoyable to retrace my steps as a writer and her steps as a singer."

Bray and Madonna first met in Ann Arbor, Michigan, in 1977 when both were still students at the University of Michigan. Bray said the pair became romantically involved before working together professionally.

"We're an off and on (in romance) for that period there in Michigan and a little bit in New York," Bray said. "It was like dating any college student. I think in that respect she's no different from anybody else. Women are women."
A few years later, Bray joined Madonna's band "Emmy" as a drummer. The band played in the style of popular bands like "The Pretenders," "The Police" and "Blondie."
"When we started to write together it turned into a more danceable ... thing," Bray said. "We had high hopes."
Soon the pair began recording the songs which would form the basis for Madonna's trademark dance beat music and which appear on "Pre-Madonna."
Bray, who worked with a number of bands around that time, said Madonna stood out as the prospect most likely to succeed.

"I knew that of all the people I was working with (Madonna) was the best shot because nobody else had her kind of energy or her kind of drive," he said. "She clearly stood out as somebody who was consumed by desire."

Although the pair had a falling out when Madonna found another producer for her debut recording in 1982, the two eventually got back together and worked on a string of hits, "Like A Virgin," "True Blue," "Who's That Girl" and "Like A Prayer."
Bray produced and wrote many of Madonna's biggest hits until they finally parted company in 1989.
"I suppose we could have kept working together but I was getting into that California 'finding yourself' thing," Bray said. "By that time I was tired after 10 years of working constantly."
